title: Garbled Garden
statementMd:
After an extremely tiring day at work, Tessa arrived home to find her husband waiting proudly at the door. With a huge smile on his face, he announced that he had planted all her flowers in the garden. Grateful that her husband had taken some work off her shoulders, she went straight out to the garden. Her relief lasted exactly until she reached it.

While he did indeed manage to plant all of her flowers around the edge of the garden, unfortunately, the arrangement was very wrong. Roses stood where the orchids should have been. Hyacinths, dahlias, and chrysanthemums were scattered among the hydrangeas. The whole garden looked as though a toddler had planted them.

Tessa stared at the numbered tags still tied to the stems. She had arduously labelled every single flower with non-decreasing labels from left to right of the intended order. Flowers of the same species had matching tags since the order within one type of flower did not matter.

Her husband followed her gaze to the labels, shrugged, and said he thought that they were price tags and had not paid any attention to them ...

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/9e1f2b6209d7373f075c6e101c2f9bd617fbc2f8.png) ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/6e57e07b9ba3c849e02bc268d204f648aba29963.png)![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ea1800860f294819e012eab27d7680ba60ce5f98.png) ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f13171dc01a2e9d931b428cf80b8b228a5732b8b.png)Visualization of the second sample answer.

Sighing, she settled down and decided to fix this mess. Since the flowers were still very young and delicate, she cannot just dig out some of the flowers, rearrange them, and then plant them back. Instead, she can do the following operation:

- She chooses an integer $m$ and a sequence of $m$ distinct integers $p_1, \dots, p_m$.
- First, she picks the flower at position $p_1$ and moves it back into a flowerpot.
- Then, she repeatedly chooses the flower at position $p_i$ ($i \geq 2$), and moves it to the now empty position $p_{i-1}$ of the previous flower.
- Finally, after $m-1$ iterations of the previous step, she finishes the operation by replanting the potted flower at the remaining empty position $p_m$.

Every flower can be used at most once within the same operation due to their fragile nature.

Determine the minimum number of operations Tessa has to do to fix the arrangement, and output one possible sequence of these operations.

## Input

The input consists of:

- One line with an integer $n$ ($2 \leq n \leq 5000$), the number of Tessa's flowers.
- One line with $n$ integers $t_1, \ldots, t_n$ ($1 \leq t_i \leq n$ for each $i$), where $t_i$ is the tag number of the flower at position $i$.

## Output

First, output the minimum number of operations $k$ ($0 \leq k \leq n$) to fix the arrangement. It can be proven that there always is an answer taking at most $n$ operations.

Then, for each of the $k$ operations, output:

- One integer $m$ ($1 \leq m \leq n$), the number of flowers moved in this operation.
- $m$ distinct integers $p_1, \ldots, p_m$ ($1 \leq p_i \leq n$ for each $i$), the positions of the flowers used in this operation. The order should match the order they are used in this operation.

Note that only the number of operations has to be minimal, not the number of flowers involved.

If there are multiple optimal solutions, you may output any one of them.
statementZhMd:
在度过了极其疲惫的一天工作后，Tessa 回到家，发现丈夫正得意地在门口等着她。他满脸笑容地宣布，自己已经把她所有的花都种进了花园。Tessa 很感激丈夫替她分担了一些工作，便径直走向花园。然而，刚走到花园，她就再也轻松不起来了。

丈夫确实把她所有的花都种在了花园边缘，但不幸的是，花的排列完全不对。该种兰花的地方种着玫瑰，风信子、大丽花和菊花混杂在绣球花之间。整个花园看起来就像是一个蹒跚学步的孩子种出来的。

Tessa 盯着那些仍系在花茎上的数字标签。她曾费尽心思，按照预定的排列顺序，从左到右为每一株花标上了不递减的编号。同一种花的标签编号相同，因为同种花之间的顺序并不重要。

丈夫顺着她的目光看向那些标签，耸了耸肩，说他以为那些是价格标签，所以完全没有在意……

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/9e1f2b6209d7373f075c6e101c2f9bd617fbc2f8.png) ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/6e57e07b9ba3c849e02bc268d204f648aba29963.png)![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ea1800860f294819e012eab27d7680ba60ce5f98.png) ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f13171dc01a2e9d931b428cf80b8b228a5732b8b.png)第二个样例答案的示意图。

她叹了口气，定下心来，决定收拾这个烂摊子。由于这些花还很幼小、娇嫩，她不能直接挖出一些花，重新排列后再种回去。她可以改为执行以下操作：

- 选择一个整数 $m$ 和一个由 $m$ 个互不相同的整数组成的序列 $p_1, \dots, p_m$。
- 首先，将位置 $p_1$ 的花移回花盆中。
- 然后，依次选取位置 $p_i$（$i \geq 2$）的花，将其移到上一株花移走后空出的位置 $p_{i-1}$。
- 最后，在上一步执行 $m-1$ 次后，将花盆中的花重新种到唯一剩余的空位置 $p_m$，结束本次操作。

由于花十分脆弱，同一次操作中，每株花最多只能被使用一次。

请确定 Tessa 至少需要执行多少次操作才能将花排列正确，并输出一种可行的操作序列。

## 输入格式

输入包括：

- 一行，包含一个整数 $n$（$2 \leq n \leq 5000$），表示 Tessa 的花的数量。
- 一行，包含 $n$ 个整数 $t_1, \ldots, t_n$（对于每个 $i$，都有 $1 \leq t_i \leq n$），其中 $t_i$ 表示位置 $i$ 的花的标签编号。

## 输出格式

首先，输出将花排列正确所需的最少操作次数 $k$（$0 \leq k \leq n$）。可以证明，总存在一个至多执行 $n$ 次操作的方案。

然后，对于这 $k$ 次操作中的每一次，输出：

- 一个整数 $m$（$1 \leq m \leq n$），表示本次操作移动的花的数量。
- $m$ 个互不相同的整数 $p_1, \ldots, p_m$（对于每个 $i$，都有 $1 \leq p_i \leq n$），表示本次操作使用的花的位置。输出顺序应与本次操作中使用它们的顺序一致。

注意，只需要使操作次数最少，无须使涉及的花的数量最少。

如果存在多个最优方案，你可以输出其中任意一个。
